title: AlloyDB: where it fits between Cloud SQL and Spanner

videos.script: AlloyDB speaks PostgreSQL, and your application will not notice the difference. The difference is underneath, in the storage. {{engine}} A Cloud SQL instance has a disk of its own. An AlloyDB cluster has one storage layer, shared by every machine in it, across the zones of the region. {{storage}} The primary writes only the log. The storage layer turns the log into pages, and every node reads those pages. {{log}} So a read node copies nothing, and adding one adds no storage to the bill. But there is still one writer, and that is where Spanner begins. {{writer}} Then the columnar engine. On a plain PostgreSQL you will measure what an analyst's report costs a row store. It reads the whole table to use three columns. {{columns}} AlloyDB has no emulator, so you will practise on PostgreSQL itself, and the AlloyDB parts are read from Google's documentation. {{honest}} Last, the bill. The same database priced as AlloyDB and as Cloud SQL, with a program you can check, and the amount of data where the two meet. {{bill}}
